newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says dlr above 127.16 yen, highest since 1992.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says dlr above 127.16 yen, highest since 1992.

text.p: The dollar rose above 127.16 yen in Tokyo on Thursday, the Bank of Japan (BOJ) said, its highest level against the yen since August 1992.
According to the BOJ, the dollar rose as high as 127.18 yen in morning Tokyo trade.
It rose to the high in early Tokyo trading after climbing overnight following the release of U.S. gross domestic product data which showed surprisingly robust U.S. economic growth.
The Commerce Department on Wednesday reported that the economy grew at an annual rate of 5.6 percent during the first three months of this year -- its fastest clip in more than nine years.

Dealers said option-linked selling to avoid hitting knock-out options points at around 127.30 yen had weighed on the dollar against the yen, and the greenback could rise even further if it clearly breaks through 127.30 yen.
But wariness about possible dollar-sales intervention also remains, which is likely to limit the dollar's gains, dealers added.
